name: relative math in handlers: +=, -=, *=
status: LOCKED and built (patch_relative.py + replacement cascade_plan.py / cascade_vocab.json); verified on Godot 4.3 with the stand-in mule, not yet on real Gemma
motivating_intent: when the player's item rect changes, increase its speed by 50

block_change.default: = when absent (existing blocks stay valid); allowed only with body assign; joins property, type and value as an optional slot
block_change.meaning: type is the property's type; value is the operand; the harness writes  <property> <operator> <literal>

operand_type.int: int for + - *   (Godot's parse check lets  hp += 1.5  through on an int, so GI_1 must demand an int)
operand_type.Vector2 / Vector3: the same vector type for + -;  a float scalar for *
refused_in_v1: division /= (division by zero is accepted by the parse check and gives inf or an engine error)

block_change.no_effect_refused: += 0, -= 0, *= 1 and a zero vector change nothing, so GI_1 refuses them: a handler that does nothing is not what was asked for

plan_steps.repeat_note: relative changes compound each time the signal fires. cascade_vocab.json gets a repeats flag per signal; the catalog and the dry run say 'item_rect_changed can fire many times: each time speed grows by 50.0'. ready, tree_entered, tree_exiting and tree_exited fire once per life; every other signal is flagged as repeating (unknown ones too).
plan_steps.scene_values: for 'make the starting speed 350' the harness still uses set_property with an absolute number it reads from the catalog (relative math is a runtime thing)

accepted: <property> = <property> <op> <operand>   speed = speed + 50.0   (the same statement, written long; + - * only)
GI_3.rule: operand checked as a typed literal against the block's value, exactly as for plain assignment; expressions, a second statement, other operators and comments are refused
GI_3.canonical: the harness always writes the compound form  speed += 50.0  to disk

probe.why_it_changes: a relative handler's result depends on the value it starts from, and on how many times it runs. Plain assignment did not care.
probe.isolate: in the probe's scene copies: disconnect every other _on_ handler of the node (the one under test stays, the control disconnects that one too) and switch the node's own processing off, so nothing else can move the property
probe.baseline: set the property to a known value before the stimulus: 100.0 / 100 for numbers, [10, 20] or [10, 20, 30] for vectors
probe.expected: final value = fold(baseline, operator, operand, n) where n is the emission count the spy measured in the normal run (1 for a direct call or an explicit emit); the control run must stay at the baseline; no other registered property may change
probe.hand_written_handlers: a handler body that is a plain compound statement is read back from the script and verified the same way; anything else stays UNVERIFIED

parse_check_lets_through_wrongly: hp += 1.5 and hp *= 1.5 on an int property
tested_on_godot_4_3.fold: from 100: += 50.0 gives 150; two more calls give 250 (each emission adds); *= 1.5 gives 150; velocity (10,20) += (0,10) gives (10,30); hp 5 *= 2 gives 10
tested_on_godot_4_3.drift: with the scene running for 4 frames velocity stayed (10,20) while position moved; switching the node's physics processing off is a cheap guard for scenes where physics does change velocity

open_slots_after_step_12: operands that are expressions or other properties
decisions_to_lock: 1. the operator slot with the operand rules and the no-effect refusal
2. the plan steps increase / decrease / scale, and the repeat note in the catalog and the dry run
3. GI_3 accepting the compound, self. and long forms, with the compound form written to disk
4. the probe: isolation, known baseline, expected = fold over the measured emission count, control stays at baseline
5. delivery: patch_relative.py for the clock and the spec (per-file, with the patch library) plus replacement cascade_plan.py and cascade_vocab.json
